# Copilot instructions for reddish_hermit

This file helps Copilot-style assistants work effectively in this repository. Keep it short and actionable.

---

## Build, test, and lint (how developers run things locally)

Prerequisites: conan, CMake, a C++20 toolchain (CI uses gcc-11/g++-11 on Ubuntu 22.04).

Common full workflow (Debug):

1. Install dependencies and generate CMake presets:
   - conan install . --build=missing -s build_type=Debug --output-folder=build
2. Configure (uses presets generated by conan):
   - cmake . --preset conan-debug
3. Build:
   - cmake --build --preset conan-debug
4. Run tests (ctest uses the same preset):
   - ctest --preset conan-debug

Helper scripts (CI uses these):
- script/build_client.sh <Debug|Release> — runs conan install + cmake configure with -DENABLE_CLIENT=ON + build
- script/build_server.sh <Debug|Release> — same but with -DENABLE_SERVER=ON

Run a single test by name (after configure+build):
- ctest --preset conan-debug -R connection_test

Notes about tests and lint:
- Tests are gated by the CMake option ENABLE_TEST (default: ON).
- When ENABLE_TEST is ON targets are compiled with: -fsanitize=address -g --coverage -Wall -Wextra -Werror — warnings are treated as errors.
- There is no checked-in CMakePresets.json; conan install generates presets (conan-debug, conan-release). Always run conan install first.

---

## High-level architecture

- common/ — Header-first common library (reddish_hermit_common) that provides:
  - network::Connection (buffered reads/writes, timeout support)
  - protocol/RESP reader & writer
  - command parsing and utility helpers
  This library is depended on by both the client and server.

- client/ — Client library (reddish_hermit_client). Async awaitable API built on Boost.ASIO coroutines.

- server/ — Server executable (reddish_hermit_server). Contains kiedis, storage, and command implementations.

- Build: CMake + Conan. Sources are gathered in each component using aux_source_directory in src/CMakeLists.txt; adding a .cpp under an existing src dir is picked up automatically.

- Tests: gtest + coroutine tests live under common/test. The only real test currently checked in is common/test/connection/connection_test.cpp; other test CMake files are placeholders.

- CI: .github/workflows/cmake.yml uses script/build_client.sh and script/build_server.sh and runs ctest --preset conan-debug.

---

## Key codebase conventions and gotchas

- Namespaces: use `reddish::common::...`, `reddish::server::...`, `reddish::client::...`.
- Naming: snake_case is the common style for symbols in code.
- Coroutines: code uses Boost.ASIO coroutines heavily (co_await). Many functions return awaitable wrappers (boost::asio::awaitable<T>). Tests and code assume an executor context.
- Protocol (RESP): common/protocol contains RESP reader/writer. The project currently implements RESP2 semantics; care is taken to be allocation-minimal and to preserve performance.
- Auto-sources: src/CMakeLists use aux_source_directory — adding files under an existing src/ directory is picked up automatically; adding new directories requires updating CMakeLists.
- Tests build flags: enabling tests toggles -Werror and sanitizers; fix warnings first — builds will fail otherwise.
- No checked-in CMake presets: do not expect .cmakepresets.json in the repo; run conan install to create presets used by CI.

---

## Where to look for common tasks

- Add protocol changes: common/src/protocol and common/include/common/protocol
- Add network/IO changes: common/src/connection and common/include/common/network
- Tests: common/test
- CI build scripts: script/*.sh and .github/workflows/cmake.yml
- Packaging: conanfile.py
